original_question: Is every Sylow-metacyclic finite group Q-admissible, that is, realizable as the Galois group of a maximal subfield of some crossed-product division algebra over Q?
target_in_paper: Problem 11.2 in §11.A (the "Q-admissibility conjecture"): Prove every Sylow-metacyclic group is Q-admissible.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended target very closely: it fixes the base field to Q, asks about the Sylow-metacyclic hypothesis, uses the paper's notion of Q-admissibility, and correctly paraphrases admissibility in terms of realizing the group as the Galois group of a maximal subfield of a crossed-product division algebra over Q. This is essentially the content of Problem 11.2 in §11.A.
missing_details: The paper quantifies over a finite group G; using Q as the group symbol is potentially confusing because Q is the base field of rationals.
The paper's exact hypothesis is that G is Sylow-metacyclic, meaning every Sylow subgroup of G is metacyclic.
For a stand-alone formulation, 'metacyclic' should be unpacked as: each Sylow subgroup P has a cyclic normal subgroup N with cyclic quotient P/N.
The paper defines Q-admissible via the existence of a G-crossed-product Q-division algebra, not merely an arbitrary division algebra over Q.
To be fully self-contained, one should say that a Q-division algebra is central over Q.
The crossed-product condition should be stated explicitly as the existence of a maximal subfield L of the division algebra such that L/Q is Galois with Gal(L/Q) isomorphic to G.
The question should remain the special case K = Q of the broader admissibility problem in Problem 11.1, rather than drifting to arbitrary number fields.
refined_question: Let G be a finite group such that every Sylow subgroup of G is metacyclic (equivalently, for each prime p dividing |G|, a Sylow p-subgroup P of G has a cyclic normal subgroup N with cyclic quotient P/N). Must G be Q-admissible; that is, does there exist a central division algebra D over Q having a maximal subfield L such that L/Q is Galois and Gal(L/Q) ≅ G?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, is every finite Sylow-metacyclic group G the Galois group of a maximal subfield of some G-crossed-product Q-division algebra?
justification: The draft is aiming at §11.A, Problem 11.2, which the paper explicitly calls the Q-admissibility conjecture. The nearby definition in §11.A says what K-admissible means for a finite group G, and §0 supplies the definition of crossed product in terms of containing a maximal subfield that is Galois over the center. The surrounding context in §11.A also explains why the Sylow-metacyclic condition is the exact one appearing in the conjecture: Schacher's theorem shows that every Q-admissible group is Sylow-metacyclic, motivating the converse problem stated as Problem 11.2. So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is the finite-group, base-field-Q version above, without broadening to arbitrary number fields.

citations.label: What is known (Schacher's necessity of the Sylow-metacyclic condition)
